name: Kaspersky — Network Attack Detected Against an Endpoint
description:
Attacker objective
Exploit a network-facing service on an endpoint or server (remote code execution, scanning, brute-force) for initial access or lateral movement.

Attack logic
Kaspersky Network Threat Protection (host network IPS) detects and blocks known network exploits and attacks directed at the protected host.

Why this detection works
The attack signature name, the victim host and the attacker IP together are a high-fidelity indicator that an exploitation attempt reached the host.

False positives
An authorised vulnerability scanner triggering network-attack signatures.

Tuning
Allowlist sanctioned scanner sources; prioritise attacks targeting servers over workstations.

Required telemetry
Kaspersky Security Center CEF (GNRL_EV_ATTACK_DETECTED): AttackName, destination.domain (victim), AttackerIPv4, AttackedPort/Protocol.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. The attack name, victim host (destination.domain) and attacker IP are in the event.
2. Confirm whether the targeted service is exposed; even if blocked, profile the attacker and hunt for follow-on activity on the victim.
3. Prioritise attacks against internet-facing or high-value servers.
false_positives: An authorised vulnerability scanner triggering network-attack signatures.
